entry.name: Grasp Like Humans
entry.title: Grasp Like Humans: Learning Generalizable Multi-Fingered Grasping from Human Proprioceptive Sensorimotor Integration
entry.summary: Two demonstrators wore a data glove with 25 printed force-sensitive pads (ROXIFSR) and a Noitom PN3 Pro inertial hand tracker for 150 ten-second grasp-and-lift trials of 5 objects, with left and right hands.
entry.hand: Custom data glove: 25-pad printed FSR array (ROXIFSR) + Noitom PN3 Pro (6 IMUs)

sensor.note: Per pad <name>_Tactile_Feedback: raw ADC value of the contact-force magnitude (readme.pdf). Rest ~1,100-1,800 counts, rising by up to ~1,100 in a grasp; maximum in the release 3,687. Pads on the distal, middle and proximal phalanges and metacarpal of each finger plus the lower palm (paper Fig. 3). 15 Hz in the release; the array samples above 200 Hz (paper).

scale.text: 150 trials x 10 s (152 samples at 15 Hz), 5 objects, 2 demonstrators, left and right hands, side and top-down grasps

entry.access: One 21 MB zip linked as 'Dataset' on the project page (GitHub Pages), no login.
caveats: Only the training demonstrations are released: 5 seen objects. The 15 unseen test objects and the robot-hand trials with the glove are not included.
No video, timestamps or object pose: one CSV per 10 s trial.
Tactile values are raw ADC counts with a non-zero rest level (~1,100-1,800); the paper calibrates pads with standard weights but the conversion is not released.
The root joint position (Hand_Joint_Posi_X/Y/Z) is constant within a trial and Bone_Length columns are constants from the PN3 Pro skeleton template.
File numbering differs between folders (group1-group15 vs group01-group30).

tracking.note: 20 hand joints: Euler angles, joint positions, bone angle and angular velocity; ~70 Hz native (paper), 15 Hz in the release

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.08354 (Sec. III-A, IV, VI-A, Table I)
unconfirmed: hours and frames derived: 150 CSVs x 152 rows at 15 Hz = 22,800 samples, 1,520 s.
subjects=2 from readme.pdf: GC (male, 180 cm, hand length 18.5 cm) and YH (female, 165 cm, 15.5 cm).
tasks=1: grasp and lift; grasp mode (side or top-down) is fixed per object.
Paper: 30 grasps per object; in the release carambola is split 15 left / 15 right hand (GC) and football 15 GC right / 15 YH left.
Contact check: pad 'rise' = mean of the last 5 s minus mean of the first 10 samples; all 150 trials show pads rising during the grasp.
NUDT (National University of Defense Technology) is a Chinese university; the release has no Chinese names, so no zh entry.
Zip members dated 2025-07-14; project repository last pushed 2025-09-11; the repository README licenses only the website (CC BY-SA 4.0).

sample.fetch_estimate: 21 MB (the whole zip, already fetched under the survey scratch directory); episode JSON ~0.2 MB each; no media.
sample.rules_applied: 5 objects, each a grasp-and-lift task (<= 6), so all 5 are taken, one trial each; with 4-5 tasks one episode per task. The picks cover both hands (right for carambola) and both demonstrators (YH for football). Within each folder the trial with the most pads rising more than 200 counts (last 5 s vs first 10 samples) was chosen. Trials are 10.1 s, within 10-60 s.
